Imagine serving a multi-year prison sentence in just a matter of minutes! Scientists have developed a method to implant artificial memories, making prisoners believe they have served years behind bars. This revolutionary approach promises to reduce costs and alleviate overcrowding in prisons.

But is it all too good to be true? What are the potential downsides of such a technology? Let’s talk about the ethical, psychological, and societal implications.
